account: It is ten o'clock on day 0, and I am at the plaza for my scheduled market walk. So far I have no concrete evidence of anything unusual. My feeling that something is happening without me remains only a suspicion. The secretary reported no correspondence or unusual concerns, retrieved the appointment book after I returned it, and said it was secured. That appears to be ordinary scheduling work, not evidence of secrecy. Townsfolk 30 and 20 both told me they had no news. Townsfolk 10 is nearby but I have not yet asked them. I now see the builder walking near the market carrying a lantern; I do not know their destination or purpose, and carrying a lantern alone is no reason to suspect anything. I heard the secretary speaking as I left, but could not distinguish the words, so I cannot draw conclusions from that. My remaining engagements today are lunch at home at noon, office accounts at one, tea with the neighbour at a dockside cottage on the east bank at three, office at four thirty, and home at seven. I should keep those appointments while gathering ordinary, firsthand news from residents rather than treating guesses as facts.
